properties.Location: South Side of Santa Rosa Island, Between Ford Point and South Point
properties.IncidentOverview: On Friday; May 15; 2026; an aircraft flying over Santa Rosa Island in Channel Islands National Park reported a wildfire. National Park Service (NPS) staff already on the island confirmed it later that morning. The Santa Rosa Island Fire is located on the southeastern end of the island in remote and rugged terrain. This is a full-suppression human-caused wildfire and is under investigation. Current Situation: Today was another very active day on the fire with most of the activity on the northeast side of the fire. A combination of wind and terrain are the primary drivers of the activity; and the fire grew to 14;520 acres today. Strong northeast winds; typical of a Santa Ana wind event; produced wind gusts over 30 mph on the island. Fire crews were able to complete additional defensible space preparations around structures on the northeast side of the island such as the ranger station; Vail and Vickers Ranch Historic District including the main ranch house and island infrastructure like the fuel building. Structures also include the maintenance area; utilities; pier; bridges; campgrounds; and an historic schoolhouse. Heavy equipment operators are also in place assisting with the defensible space improvements. Additionally; firefighters have made progress prepping Main (Soledad) Road and Telephone Road to be used for potential strategic firing operations as part of an indirect confinement strategy if conditions allow and it is safe to do so. Firefighters are also prepared to do any defensive firing tonight from the Water Canyon Campground if conditions require it to protect that area. Unfortunately; the fire has reached the Torrey Pines area on the east side of the island. Upon initial assessments; fire crews are observing that the fire intensity was low and that the stand remains intact. When safe to do so; a fire effects crew will be assigned to make a full determination of condition and any long-term effect On the southwest side of the fire; firefighters are working on improving defensible space around the lighthouse at South Point and establishing an anchor point to build more containment line at that corner of the fire. This morning; aircraft flew over the island to assess the potential for water drops by air tankers but with the strong winds; those water drops would have still been ineffective. In addition; today new wildfires ignited on the mainland which immediately became the priority. Per policy; firefighting resources are always assigned based on the greatest threats to life; safety; and property. This prioritization helps ensure that the most urgent needs are addressed first during rapidly evolving fire activity. Tomorrow; additional firefighters and equipment such as additional UTV’s; fire hose and pumps will be arriving to the island along with resupplies for the firefighters already on the island. The incident management team is also working on getting specialized wildland fire engines onto the island by midweek to engage in the firefighting effort. Closures: The National Park Service has closed Santa Rosa Island to day use and overnight use at least through this week due to the wildfire. Visitors with campground reservations at Water Canyon Campground have been notified via e-mail. Structures: There are two uninhabited historic structures in the area; Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed on the western edge; and Wreck Line Camp Cabin on the eastern edge. Unfortunately; both have been confirmed destroyed. An additional storage structure was also destroyed adjacent to Johnson’s Lee Equipment Shed.
